[88] Now let’s take what we have learned and apply it to a distinctly Canadian perspective. Are the Indigenous peoples of Canada being discriminated against at an institutional level? Does the discrimination, stereotyping and racism experienced by Indigenous peoples meet the criteria set forth by your textbook and the website above regarding institutionalized discrimination?
[94] Follow the link to read the January 15th, 2015 MacLean’s article titled, Canada’s race problem? It’s even worse than America’s, by Scott Gilmore.
[102] Follow the link to read the CTV News article titled, Aboriginal Canadians face racism, stereotyping in urban health care: report
[109] Utilizing the resources above, or your own research, answer the following questions in paragraph form.

Does the discrimination, stereotyping and racism experienced by Indigenous peoples meet the criteria set forth by your textbook and the website above regarding institutionalized discrimination? (ensure to cite all sources used)
[159] What do you think about Canada 150 celebrations? Are they a celebration of colonialism? Why or why not? (2 Marks)
[185] Assignment 3.2 Reel Injun, by filmmaker Neil Diamond /24
[212] Head to Aboriginal Studies 30 in Moodle to watch the documentary titled Reel Injun, by Catherine Bainbridge, Neil Diamond and Jeremiah Hayes.
[214] While watching the documentary, you will respond to the following chapter discussion questions. You will notice questions for several chapters of the documentary have been omitted. You are still responsible for watching the entire piece. For the purpose of this course, you only need to respond to what is asked.
[215] *Questions taken from NFB.com
[217] ***NOTE: In these questions & main point summaries, the terms Indian, First Nations, Aboriginals, Indigenous Peoples, Natives, Native American & politically incorrect “Injun” are used in reference to the filmmakers’ choice & style of script writing. These terms are not meant to be insensitive in any way to modern correct terminology.
[219] ***NOTE: Generally speaking, Indigenous peoples do not have a European version of a NATIONAL borders; therefore, in many cases terminology will transcend geopolitical borders. South of the 49th parallel, in the United States the term Native American is an acceptable and common term to describe Indigenous peoples. Because this filmmaker is analyzing the Hollywood perspective, American (USA) terminology regarding Indigenous peoples is ever present in this piece.
[222] Native Representation Reel Injun – Chapter 1
[224] What are the consequences of distorted representations of Indigenous people with regard to their identity, self-esteem and social and cultural development?
[228] One hundred years of cinema have shaped the folkloric images of Native Americans to the point that some people believe that Indians (Indigenous peoples) still live in teepees. But what is an “Injun” in 2011?
[234] The Good Indian The Noble Injun – Chapter 3
[236] The silent era portrayed Native people as noble; how did that come to be?
[243] Why are some people excited by the idea of being Native regardless of the bad image projected by Hollywood?
[248] Do you think that the kids in the summer camp sequence in Reel Injun were only encountered Native people in Hollywood movies?
[253] According to Hollywood’s criteria, what does it take to be a good or noble Indian?
[258] Tonto speech and stereotypes The savage Injun – Chapter 4
[260] By developing the Tonto speech, did Hollywood harm the existing Native languages spoken by US tribes?
[264] Robbing nations of their identity is an act of colonialism, but why did the Plains Indians attract more attention than the Pawnees or the Mohawks?
[268] What are some of the misguided notions surrounding the Indian princess Pocahontas?
[273] A violent and Racist Icon The Cowboy – Chapter 5
[275] When John Wayne shoots a dead Indian that was dug up from a burial ground in the eyes to make sure he will not be going to the spirit world, what kind of message is Hollywood sending?
[280] What about the use of Native languages in the movies: Is it desirable in order to improve the pride and self-esteem of First Nations people?
[286] Indians or human Beings? A Good Injun . . is it a Dead Injun? – Chapter 6
[288] Retrace the history and the meaning of this famously racist pronouncement by General Philip Sheridan: “A Good Injun . . . is a Dead Injun.” Why would Hollywood use such neo-colonialist propaganda to confuse the feelings of young Native people?
[292] Regarding the notion of human beings, why does John Trudell place so much emphasis on language as an instrument of war?
[296] What does it mean to you to be a human being?
[301] No More stereotypes and stoic Indians The Renaissance – Chapter 8
[304] Director Neil Diamond mentioned that he found the answers he was looking for in the North. What exactly was the object of his quest?
[308] On what basis can we say that Atanarjuat is the “most Native” movie ever made?
[356] Assignment 3.2 Stereotypes & Bias/20
[364] Brainstorm alternative names and symbols for sports teams that currently use Aboriginal stereotypes or cultural objects inappropriately.
[370] Present a report on your findings and write a letter to the owner of the team requesting a change in team names. Your report must include:
[372] You must include the basic history of the issue
[373] Any demonstrations, political or civil activism regarding the offensive name
[374] Any pending legal actions
[375] A solution to the issue
[376] A letter to the owner
[378] You can present your report via any medium you wish, but ensure your letter to the owner is included with your report. Please share any multimedia projects with your instructor.
[382] Assessment Criteria 20 marks
[384] Included history of the issue 2 marks
[385] Provided solution to the issue 2 marks
[386] Included a bibliography of all resources used/cited for assignment 3 marks
[387] The response has been organized appropriately. 2 marks
[388] The response has been skilfully revised and edited. 2 marks
[389] Included any/all relevant information ex: legal issues, civil activism etc 3 marks
[390] Includes Letter to the Owner 4 marks
[400] Life in Rural Aboriginal Communities
[402] Read pages 180 - 188 of your textbook to complete the following questions.
[424] Why do some First Nations people choose to live on reserves? What are the major benefits of reserve life? (4 Marks)
[428] List Factors that might make a First nations person choose to leave a reserve and move to a city? (4 Marks)
[432] List factors that can make it difficult for Aboriginal people used to life in Aboriginal communities to make the transition to life in an urban center.  (4 Marks)
[443] Read pages 188 - 198 of your textbook to complete the following questions.
[445] Why do some First Nations people move back to reserves, even if they are adapting well to life in a city? (2 Marks)
[450] What are the challenges and benefits of developing resources in Aboriginal communities? (3 Marks)
[461] Read pages 198 - 204 of your textbook to complete the following questions.
[463] Why do some non-Aboriginal people object to special government services for Aboriginal people? In a table, list some of the arguments in one column. In the second column, examine each argument from an Aboriginal perspective. /8
[481] What factors can affect a community’s ability to deliver it own services? (2 Marks)
[486] What roles do Friendship Centres play in the urban community? (2 Marks)
[530] Assignment 3.3 Attawapiskat Report
[532] Using the articles above and at least three others you source yourself, report on the economic conditions for the Attawapiskat reserve.
[534] Your report must include:
[535] Current data dated at least 2015 and above
[536] Information regarding the suicide crisis
[537] A plan that would involve the people of Attawapiskat in the design, delivery and administration of services to the community to help develop healing and prosperity.
[539] You can present your report via any medium you wish. Please share any multimedia projects with your instructor.
[541] Assessment Criteria 20 marks
[543] • Includes bibliography (3 sources minimum) 4 marks
[544] • Essential information has been included. 6 marks
[545] • Includes a community based plan 6 marks
[546] • Creativity 2 marks
[547] • The response has been skilfully revised and edited. 2 marks
[551] Assignment 3.4 Protests/20
[553] Between 1951 and 2000 – how many Indigenous protests have there been across Turtle Island, specifically Canada?
[555] Choose one of the protests and create a detailed report regarding the following:
[557] Who are the main organizers? Include Bios and pictures
[558] What is the background of the protest? (5 W’s)
[559] What is/was the outcome of the protest (if at all)?
[561] If you are stuck getting started, here are a few options, but feel free to choose any protest organized by Indigenous peoples across Turtle Island (Canada preferred).
[563] Ipperwash
[564] Oka
[565] Idle No More
[566] Elijah Harper and Meech Lake Accord
[567] Resistance 150
[568] Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women (Say Her Name)
[569] Standing Rock
[571] You can present your report via any medium you wish. Please share any multimedia projects with your instructor.
[574] Assessment Criteria 20 marks
[576] • Ideas are insightful. 4 marks
[577] • Includes bibliography 3 marks
[578] • Essential information has been included. 9 Marks

[580] • The response has been skilfully revised and edited. 2 marks

[628] Find biographical information about the individual. Read a minimum of two works (if they are an author, include one of their own pieces). These can be: short stories, news articles, peer reviewed article (published by a university), biographies, letters or any other publications from the individual or about the individual.  The more you read, the better your understanding will be.
[629] Create a profile of your individual and include the answers to the following questions:
[630] What biographical information did you find about the person?
[631] Who are they? What are they known for? What did they do (or try to do)?
[632] Are there any specific issues they have been activists for?
[633] What projects have they worked on?
[634] How has this person been influenced by his or her life experiences or those of family or community members?
[635] If they are an artist, how is a specifically aboriginal experience portrayed in this person’s work?
[636] What purpose or message does this person voice?
[637] In your opinion, what are the significant contributions of this person to Indigenous communities and settler society?
[640] Your profile can be presented in any form of your choice, but it MUST include a visual component. This can be a set of 4 banners on a string highlighting your findings, or a scrapbook with your findings and photos of all four leaders. Be creative! Please share your project to your instructor.
